reference.title: The patient’s dream
reference.text: A patient tells a psychoanalyst, Dr Melloni, about his dream: a party, champagne, a garden with flowers, somebody playing the violin, an owl in a tree, and very cold feet. Dr Melloni then interprets each thing in the dream.

tasks.instruction: Ask and answer the questions about dreams
tasks.note: SB 1a → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: Speaking practice in an English class (level: pre-intermediate), topic dreams. Ask the student these questions one at a time, react, and answer their questions too: Do you often remember your dreams? Have you ever had the same dream more than once? Have you ever dreamed about something that then happened? Do you think dreams can tell us anything about the future?
exercises.opener: Do you often remember your dreams?
criteria: answers the four questions with details
uses the present perfect for experiences (I’ve had… / I’ve never dreamed…) and the past simple for details
asks at least one question back

steps.example: Not very often, but sometimes I remember them in the morning.

reference.title: Verb forms
rows: I live in the city centre. She doesn’t smoke.
things that always or usually happen
He’s looking for a new job. I’m leaving tomorrow.
things happening now or around now; future arrangements

reference.title: Auxiliary verbs in questions
reference.text: Each tense has its own auxiliary: Do / Does (present simple), am / is / are (present continuous, going to), Did (past simple), was / were (past continuous), will (future), have / has (present perfect).

reference.title: File 5
reference.text: Comparatives: -er / more + adjective + than; (not) as… as; less… than; adverbs: faster, more carefully. Superlatives: the -est / the most + adjective; the… I’ve ever… Quantifiers: too much + uncountable, too many + plural, too + adjective, enough + noun, adjective + enough.

reference.title: File 6
reference.text: will / won’t + infinitive for predictions (I don’t think it’ll rain), instant decisions (I’ll have the fish), offers (I’ll help you. Shall I…?) and promises (I won’t tell anybody). Review of verb forms: present simple and continuous, past simple and continuous, be going to, will, present perfect.

tasks.instruction: Can you understand this text? Read the article. How did Mahalia Jackson help Martin Luther King?
tasks.note: Revise and Check 5&6 «Can you understand this text?» a (открытый вопрос) → Blank по статье. MODEL
tasks.context:
Mahalia Jackson was a musical legend who helped to bring gospel music from the church to large audiences. She was Aretha Franklin’s mentor, and in 1961 she was the first gospel singer to win a Grammy Award. She was also an important member of the Civil Rights Movement in the USA, and she was a close friend of Martin Luther King. Mahalia often went with King on civil rights demonstrations and marches, including into the most hostile parts of the South, and she sang at the events. As a presenter from National Public Radio said, ‘her voice became the soundtrack of the Civil Rights Movement’. On 28th August 1963, there was a famous march in Washington against racism. Mahalia was with King, who was going to give a five-minute speech. Before the day itself, he and his advisers decided what he was going to say. King began speaking to an audience of more than 250,000 people. But towards the end, he felt that his speech was not going well. Suddenly Mahalia shouted ‘Tell them about the dream, Martin. Tell them about the dream’. She knew about it because she was at a previous event in Detroit, in June of that year, where King talked about his dream for African Americans. It was, in the words of King’s adviser Clarence Jones, ‘one of the world’s greatest gospel singers shouting to one of the world’s greatest preachers’. King looked at Mahalia. Then he threw away his written speech, and looked at the audience. ‘I have a dream… I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the colour of their skin, but by the content of their character…’ And so he continued, and he gave one of the best-loved speeches in American history.

Civil Rights Movement – the campaign in the 1950s and 1960s to change the laws so that African Americans have the same rights as others. preacher – a person who gives inspiring talks about religion.

Tell them about the dream’. She knew about it because she was at a previous event in Detroit, in June of that year, where King talked about his dream for African Americans. It was, in the words of King’s adviser Clarence Jones, ‘one of the world’s greatest gospel singers shouting to one of the world’s greatest preachers’. King looked at Mahalia. Then he threw away his written speech, and looked at the audience. ‘I have a dream… I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the colour of their skin, but by the content of their character…’ And so he continued, and he gave one of the best-loved speeches in American history.

Civil Rights Movement – the campaign in the 1950s and 1960s to change the laws so that African Americans have the same rights as others. preacher – a person who gives inspiring talks about religion.

exercises.situation: A friendly revision chat in an English class (level: pre-intermediate) after Files 5 and 6. Check that the student can do these things, one by one, with short questions and reactions: 1) compare two people in their family using adjectives and adverbs; 2) talk about their town or city using four superlatives; 3) talk about what they drink using (not) enough and too much / too many; 4) make three predictions about the future with will / won’t; 5) make a promise, an offer and a decision with will / won’t. Move to the next point after the student has done one. Correct gently.
exercises.goal: Show that you can do the five things from Files 5 and 6.
exercises.opener: Let’s start with your family. Can you compare two people in your family?
criteria: compares two family members with a comparative adjective and a comparative adverb
uses four superlatives about their town
uses too much / too many / (not) enough correctly about drinks
makes three predictions with will / won’t
makes a promise, an offer and a decision with will / won’t or Shall I…?

steps.text: Compare two people in your family
steps.example: My brother is older than me, but I drive more carefully than him.

steps.text: Describe your town with four superlatives
steps.example: The oldest building in my town is the church.
I drink too much coffee and I don’t drink enough water.
I think it’ll rain tomorrow. I don’t think I’ll be rich.

steps.text: Make a promise, an offer and a decision
steps.example: I’ll call you tonight. Shall I help you? I think I’ll have the pasta.
